title: Breakfast at midnight?!
_map: The farm clock (Y1–2). Big idea: time to the hour, half hour, then 5 minutes; 60 minutes in an hour, 24 in a day. Creative: plan Steve's day on a clock: when do the animals eat?
_story: Steve keeps feeding the animals at the wrong time because it can't read its clock. Ismaeel learns the two hands, o'clock and half past, counts minutes in 5s, then plans Steve's day.
_stepChain: a clock has two hands → the short hand points to the hour → long hand at 12 means o'clock → half way round is half past → the long hand counts minutes: each number is 5 more (counting in 5s) → 60 minutes in an hour → the hands go round twice a day: 24 hours → plan the day

talk.ask: Which hand tells you the hour?
talk.goodAnswer: the short hand. The long hand shows the minutes.

talk.ask: Why does the 3 on a clock mean 15 minutes?
talk.goodAnswer: each number is 5 minutes more as the long hand goes round: 5, 10, 15.

handsOn: Draw a clock and plan your own day: what time do you wake up, eat lunch and go to bed? Check them on a real clock.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Oops! I gave the chickens breakfast at midnight! Bawk! And the cows got dinner at a silly time too. Moo! Everyone's grumpy! I need to learn to read my clock!

A clock has two pointers, called hands. A short hand, and a long hand. The short hand points to the hour. When the long hand points straight up at the 12, it's exactly that hour. Short hand on 9, long hand on 12. It's 9 o'clock!
Now watch the long hand. It goes half way round the clock, down to the 6. Tick, tick, tick! Half an hour has gone by. We call this half past 9.

The long hand counts minutes. A minute is about as long as counting slowly to 60! Each number on the clock is 5 more minutes. Count in fives with me: 5, 10, 15, 20, all the way to 60 at the top! So an hour has 60 minutes.
Sheep dinner time! Baa! The short hand is on the 4. The long hand is on the 12.

question.onRight: Yes! The short hand says 4, and the long hand on 12 means o'clock. 4 o'clock!

0.mistake: read the long hand as the hour
0.hint: Which hand tells the hour: the short one, or the long one?
0.say: The long hand on 12 means o'clock. The short hand tells the hour, and it's on the 4! So it's 4 o'clock.

2.mistake: thinks half past when the long hand is at the top
2.hint: Half past is when the long hand points down at the 6. Where is it now?
2.say: For half past, the long hand points down to the 6. Here it points up at the 12. So it's 4 o'clock!

question.reveal: 4 o'clock! Dinner time for the sheep. Munch, munch!

narration.text: The short hand goes all the way round twice every day. Once in the daytime, and once in the night, while you're asleep! That makes 24 hours in a day.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Now help me plan my day! When should the chickens have breakfast? When do the cows go to sleep? Tell a grown-up your plan, and show the times on a clock!

rule.text: Short hand: hours. Long hand: minutes.
rule.ask: Which hand tells the hour? What does half past mean? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: The short hand shows the hour, and the long hand shows the minutes. Half past means the long hand is half way round, on the 6.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! The long hand points to the 3. How many minutes past is that?
bonus.reveal: 15 minutes! 5, 10, 15. We call it quarter past, because it's a quarter of the way round.
